item.description:
PalMeet 0.2.1

  • The copilot, summaries and spelling fixes now use an AI provider that works. If the one you picked has no API key (or its CLI is logged out), PalMeet uses your Claude Code login, or another working provider, and says so in Settings → AI Providers.
  • New **Meeting context** box in the live view: type the agenda, ticket, who's who, names and terms at any time. The copilot uses it immediately; the summary and spelling fixes use it afterwards. Saved with the meeting as context.md.

PalMeet 0.2.0

  • Who said what: in browser meetings with live captions on (CC), every line is named from the meeting's own captions.
  • PalMeet learns voices: name a speaker once in Review and they are recognized by voice in later meetings, including the Teams and Zoom apps (Settings → General → Who said what).
  • Separate people the speaker separation lumped together, and merge one person it split in two.
  • The live view shows whose names the meeting is providing, or reminds you to turn on captions.
  • The browser extension updates itself after PalMeet updates.

PalMeet 0.1.9

  • **Mute is respected.** With a single meeting, what you say while you're muted in the meeting no longer ends up in the transcript or the saved audio (needs the PalMeet extension for browser meetings, or Accessibility for desktop Zoom/Teams). ⌃⌥M now turns your mic off/on for the meeting.
  • **Browser windows warn you.** Recording a Chrome window captures every tab in every profile; the picker now says so and shows which Chrome profiles have the extension, with a guided "Set up…" per profile (Settings → Browser Extension).
  • **Better transcripts.** After the meeting, your AI provider fixes misheard words (names, product terms) using the meeting's context. Corrected lines show a small wand icon; right-click → Restore original. Toggle in Settings → General.
